title: Decouple runtime glue and atomic kernel upgrade paths
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Our runtime combines small 'glue' components that bind CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS shared objects at startup. This tight coupling has caused symbol collisions, unpredictable probe timings, and wide blast radius during CUTLASS/Triton upgrades. Recent incidents (Feb 2026) showed a 4–8% increase in cold-start failures during rolling upgrades when multiple variant kernels were present.

Goal: Create an isolated runtime glue layer and an atomic, verifiable kernel upgrade flow so that: (1) symbol resolution and probe work happens in a contained prelink staging step rather than during hot startup; (2) kernel bundle swaps are atomic and validated with deterministic checks; (3) canaries are supported at binary level with safe automatic rollbacks.

Scope: This ticket covers the runtime-side refactor and orchestration hooks required to perform the atomic switch. It does NOT include the CI signing pipeline (dependency ENG-176501) but will integrate with the signed-bundle artifact format. Deliverables are: a) glue-isolation shim that runs in pre-init and performs symbol namespace isolation, b) an atomic kernel switch API that swaps kernel symlink/bundle with a single rename and validation, c) prelink staging phase that runs compatibility probes under a warmed-up harness, d) canary rollout orchestration hooks and health gating for the runtime agent, e) telemetry to surface probe jitter, validation latency, and canary success rates.

Non-goals: Full redesign of the kernel packaging format or changes to CUTLASS internals. We will not change the model dispatch logic; only the loading and verification path.

Success metrics: Reduce cold-start probe-related error rate during upgrades from 4% to <0.5%, reduce probe latency variance by 60%, and enable automated rollbacks for failed canaries within 90s of detection.
acceptance_criteria: New glue-isolation shim loads external kernel bundles in a separate namespace and leaves the existing runtime API unchanged
Atomic swap API performs kernel bundle replacement with zero partially-applied states (single filesystem rename semantics) and returns deterministic verification results
Prelink staging executes the probe harness and writes a deterministic artifact of compatibility checks to /var/lib/redwood/kernel-verifications
Canary orchestration supports staggered rollout (5%, 25%, 100%) and triggers automatic rollback on repeated health failures with telemetry hooks visible in Console
Unit and integration tests covering symbol isolation, atomic swap, and rollback logic with CI coverage >= 90% for new modules
Benchmark: probe latency p50 reduced and p95 variance improved by target amounts in runtime-1.22 canary runs
tasks: Design glue-isolation shim and fallback surface (design doc + sequence diagram)
Implement prelink staging harness that runs under the runtime user and performs non-destructive probes
Add atomic-swap API with filesystem-atomic semantics and verification callback
Wire canary orchestration hooks into existing rollout code (runtime agent) and add health gating rules
Add telemetry: probe_jitter_ms, verification_latency_ms, canary_failure_rate to Console metrics
Create integration tests and staged canary job definitions for QA cluster
Coordinate with release and infra to schedule a canary window and rollback playbook
